newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gazprom pays off federal tax arrears.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom pays off federal tax arrears.

text.p: Russian natural gas monopoly RAO Gazprom has paid off all its federal tax arrears, a government spokesman said on Tuesday.
"Gazprom has completely settled its accounts with the federal government," Igor Shabdurasulov told a news conference. But Gazprom still owed money to federal bodies such as the pension fund, he said.
Shabdurasulov did not give any figures, or say to what extent Gazprom had cleared debts with regional governments.

Finance Minister Anatoly Chubais said last month Gazprom would clear all its debts by the end of June, and Energy Minister Boris Nemtsov had previously estimated its total debt at 14.8 trillion roubles ($2.57 billion).

The cash-strapped government has been putting pressure on corporate tax debtors to pay off arrears. Efforts by Gazprom, one of the biggest debtors, to raise funds have been a major factor in the recent strength of the rouble.

Gazprom, itself owed trillions of roubles by its customers, has also been trying to raise short and medium-term finance on international markets, partly to pay off the taxes. On Monday it said it had mandated Credit Lyonnais and Dresdner Kleinwort Benson to organise a bridging loan of $1.2 billion and medium term credits of $2.5 to $3 billion dollars.
